clue.text: Toll collector has catch at trap in Bleak House

parts.note: the apostle Matthew was a tax gatherer before he followed Jesus
a catch or haul of game is a bag
a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: A turnpike keeper with a snare appears in a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a character found in Dickens's Bleak House, the old artilleryman who plays the bassoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The ex-soldier and bassoon player married to the 'old girl' is a figure in that Dickens novel.

clue.text: Damn an altered version with Clark Kent by Shaw

indicators.note: an altered version of the words is a rearrangement of their letters

parts.note: Clark Kent is the mild alter ego of the comic-book superhero

explanation.surface: Someone curses a rewritten Superman story with Clark Kent supposedly penned by a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered version' rearranges DAMNAN into MANAND; the definition is loose, naming a work by its author, George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's 1903 comedy about Jack Tanner and the life force is a play written by him.

clue.text: The last one of Kirk Douglas was in Brooklyn

definitions.text: The last one of Kirk Douglas was in Brooklyn

parts.words: The last one of Kirk Douglas was in Brooklyn
parts.note: the clue alludes to a dance in a film title, echoing Last ... in Paris, set in Brooklyn instead

explanation.surface: A remark about the final film of a Hollywood star.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title Last Tango in Paris is reworked: Kirk Douglas's late film was a dance set in Brooklyn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine ballroom dance is the one named in that film title.

clue.text: Friend of Apollo terminated by frisbee

definitions.text: Friend of Apollo terminated by frisbee

parts.words: Friend of Apollo terminated by frisbee
parts.note: the god's beloved youth was killed by a thrown discus, jokingly called a frisbee

explanation.surface: A companion of the sun god is killed by a flying plastic disc.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth the Spartan youth loved by Apollo was struck dead by a discus; the flower sprang from his blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The myth makes this Spartan prince Apollo's beloved, slain by an accidentally deflected discus.

clue.text: "…smoke to roll / In dusky —— reluctant flames…" (Paradise Lost)

definitions.text: "…smoke to roll / In dusky —— reluctant flames…" (Paradise Lost)

parts.words: "…smoke to roll / In dusky —— reluctant flames…" (Paradise Lost)
parts.note: a quotation with a gap, filled by the missing word from Milton's epic

explanation.surface: A line of Milton's epic poem with one word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton writes of smoke rolling in dusky coils, the word filling the blank in Book I.

clue.text: Gradated vowels, but alas radically changed

indicators.note: letters radically changed are completely rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A lament that vowel grades have been altered at their roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radically changed' rearranges BUT ALAS; the answer is the Germanic vowel gradation of sing, sang, sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaut is the linguist's term for systematic vowel gradation in related word forms.

clue.text: Mike Leigh's loony lefties surely premature?

definitions.text: Mike Leigh's loony lefties surely premature?

parts.words: Mike Leigh's loony lefties surely premature?
parts.note: Such fruit in spring would be early, and loony means crazy

explanation.surface: A question about the left-wing eccentrics in a Mike Leigh film.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Leigh's film Nuts in May follows a pair of earnest campers; nuts ripen in autumn, so in May they would be premature.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy people are called this informally, and the word heads the Leigh film title.

clue.text: Cornerpiece of Kafka's oeuvre

definitions.meaning: the chess rook starts in a corner of the board and is popularly called a castle
one of Kafka's unfinished novels, about the land surveyor K.

explanation.definitionFit: The rook sits in the corner square, and Kafka's novel bears the name of that fortress.

clue.text: Men's registries reorganized to accommodate burgher poets

indicators.note: registers reorganized are put into a different order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: Lists of men are rearranged to make room for some town-dwelling versifiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganized' rearranges MENSREGISTRIES; the answer is the guild of craftsman-poets of Wagner's Nuremberg opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval German guild singers were tradesmen of the towns who composed verse.

clue.text: Battalion of which 1 Across believed his wife to be Colour Sergeant

definitions.text: Battalion of which 1 Across believed his wife to be Colour Sergeant

parts.words: Battalion of which 1 Across believed his wife to be Colour Sergeant
parts.note: the Bleak House veteran praised his wife as the colour sergeant of a battalion with a name meaning unrivalled

explanation.surface: A Dickens character's military tribute to his capable wife.
explanation.walkthrough: In Bleak House the old soldier calls his wife the 'Colour Sergeant of the Nonpareil battalion', a word meaning peerless.
explanation.definitionFit: The battalion named in Dickens bears a word meaning peerless or without equal.

clue.text: Exist after the queen in Boeotia

indicators.note: after places the word for existing behind the preceding article

parts.note: taken as written
to exist is to be

explanation.surface: Royal life continues after the queen dies in an ancient Greek region.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Thebe was the wife of Zethus, and the Boeotian city of Thebes was named after her.
explanation.definitionFit: The nymph who married Zethus gave her name to the chief city of Boeotia, making her its queen.

clue.text: I am no substitute for Mrs Mitchison

indicators.note: a substitute version of the words is a reshuffle of their letters

explanation.surface: A self-effacing remark about not being a stand-in for a Scottish writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substitute' rearranges IAMNO; Mrs Mitchison is the Scottish novelist with this first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish author Mitchison bore this forename, so her first name answers the clue.

clue.text: Steadfast as Shadwell's relict

definitions.meaning: Thomas Shadwell's comedy The ... Widow; a relict is a widow

explanation.definitionFit: Loyal means steadfast, and Shadwell's 1678 play is titled after a faithful widow.

clue.text: Eppie, as in Civil Service

indicators.note: in puts the short word between the letters of the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Eppie, as employed in the government service.
explanation.walkthrough: Eppie in George Eliot's Silas Marner is the daughter of Godfrey, of the squire's family.
explanation.definitionFit: In Silas Marner the foundling Eppie is by birth a daughter of the squire's family.

clue.text: Collins villain keeping ballerina's support back for composer

indicators.note: keeping means the villain holds the other piece inside him

parts.note: Count Fosco is the villain of Wilkie Collins's The Woman in White

indicators.note: back means the support is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a barre is the rail a ballet dancer holds for exercises

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel's villain keeps a dancer's rail behind him for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the rail's letters round, and 'keeping' sets them inside the Count; Alfonso Ferrabosco was an Elizabethan court composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfonso Ferrabosco and his son were composers at the English court.

clue.text: Works played in person at a social club

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Musical pieces performed in person at a members' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters running across the words 'person at a social'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonatas are instrumental compositions, works performed by musicians.

clue.text: An unhelpful name could one into nothing, thought Tristram Shandy

definitions.text: An unhelpful name could one into nothing, thought Tristram Shandy

parts.words: An unhelpful name could one into nothing, thought Tristram Shandy
parts.note: Walter Shandy held that a bad name could, as he put it, the name-used-as-verb a man into nothing

explanation.surface: A fictional father's theory that poor names ruin people.
explanation.walkthrough: In Sterne's Tristram Shandy the father insists a man could be 'Nicodemus'd into nothing' by his name; the name is used as a verb, which explains the odd grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterne's Walter Shandy cites this biblical name as one that dooms its bearer to insignificance.

clue.text: It's haunting Texas, Leiber tells us

definitions.text: It's haunting Texas, Leiber tells us

parts.words: It's haunting Texas, Leiber tells us
parts.note: Fritz Leiber's 1969 novel A ... Is Haunting Texas, echoing the Communist Manifesto

explanation.surface: A science fiction writer reports a ghost in the Lone Star State.
explanation.walkthrough: Fritz Leiber's novel A Specter Is Haunting Texas supplies the word, in its British spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or apparition is what haunts, as in Leiber's title.

clue.text: Imagine the Sassoon show

definitions.meaning: to imagine is to see in the mind's eye
Siegfried Sassoon's 1919 collection ...-Show; a cinema show

explanation.definitionFit: To envisage something is to see it in your mind, and Sassoon's collection is the Picture-Show.

clue.text: Like their forebears, they were defiantly anti 10s

parts.words: Like their forebears, they were defiantly anti 10s

explanation.surface: A rebellious second generation follows its parents in opposing something.
explanation.walkthrough: '10s' means the city of Thebes; the sons of the Seven against Thebes attacked it again and won.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend these sons of the Seven took Thebes a generation after their fathers failed.

clue.text: His work was in the devil of a state

definitions.text: His work was in the devil of a state

parts.words: His work was in the devil of a state

explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Burgess wrote the novel Devil of a State, set in an imaginary African sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Burgess wrote the 1961 novel Devil of a State.

clue.text: The Bells

parts.note: Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell were the pen names of three Yorkshire sisters

explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne first published under the pseudonyms Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell.

clue.text: Pert as Pitter's potato?

explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky and impolite are near synonyms of pert, and Ruth Pitter wrote a poem about an impolite potato.

clue.text: Hungarian writer having a ball

definitions.meaning: a ballpoint pen writes with a rolling ball

explanation.definitionFit: The ballpoint pen took its trade name from its Hungarian inventor László Bíró.

clue.text: Controversial dramatist (he is confused with ban)

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled into another order

clue.text: Astronomers may well act according to him

parts.words: Astronomers may well act according to him
parts.note: the card-game rule-writer's name is shared with the Cambridge astronomer Fred, and 'according to' him means by the rules

explanation.surface: Stargazers follow the rules of a particular authority.

clue.text: Strange Lido apparition, as he seemed to Von Aschenbach

definitions.text: as he seemed to Von Aschenbach

indicators.note: strange means the letters are arranged oddly into a new word

explanation.surface: A peculiar vision on the Venetian beach, as it appeared to Mann's writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges LIDO; in Death in Venice Aschenbach worships the boy Tadzio on the Lido beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Aschenbach adores the beautiful boy Tadzio as an object of worship.

clue.text: The vote … means nothing to women. We should be (Edna O'Brien)

parts.note: an Edna O'Brien quotation whose final word, a word for carrying weapons, is left out

clue.text: Architectural form of broadsheet's page?

explanation.surface: A question on how a newspaper page is designed.

clue.text: Mrs Gaskell's reported account of swains that commend? 7,

definitions.text: Mrs Gaskell's reported account of swains that commend? 7,

parts.words: Mrs Gaskell's reported account of swains that commend? 7,
parts.note: Shakespeare's song asks who Silvia is that all our swains commend her; Gaskell's novel names those admirers

explanation.surface: A Victorian novelist's account of praising country suitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who is Silvia?' from Two Gentlemen of Verona says 'all our swains commend her'; the swains are her admirers, and Gaskell's 1863 novel takes their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell's 1863 Whitby novel is named for the admirers of its heroine.
